hook.text: China sells surveillance technology to 80 countries.

buildup.text: Huawei, ZTE, and other firms build smart city systems with facial recognition and internet monitoring.

discovery.text: Countries in Africa, Southeast Asia, and Central Asia adopt Chinese tools to monitor citizens.

twist.text: Western tech also enables surveillance. NSO Group's Pegasus spyware was used against journalists worldwide.

climax.text: The global spread of surveillance tech means censorship is no longer a domestic policy. It's an export industry.

punchline.text: Build a censorship system. Then sell it to the world.

quiz.question: How is digital authoritarianism spreading globally?
options: Chinese and Western tech firms sell surveillance tools abroad
All countries independently develop the same systems
